result:
Writing is my way of holding time still. Each word is a small act of defiance against forgetting. I write because memory is unreliable—it edits, exaggerates, and erases—but a page remembers without judgment. It accepts every draft, every false start, every embarrassing confession. There is a particular magic in leaving a message for a future self, embedding a fragment of your mind in ink for someone you will become but do not yet know.

I keep a journal, though I rarely reread it. The value is in the act: the slow settling of scattered thoughts into a line of sentences. It is a way of making sense of my own chaos, catching the loose threads of my days and weaving them into something that at least resembles a story.

Often, I write about small things—the weight of morning light on a table, the sound of rain on the roof, the particular way someone laughs. These are the details that disappear. We record the milestones: weddings, promotions, graduations. But we forget the quiet, immeasurable moments that actually make up a life.

Writing is also a way of connecting. When I write honestly, I offer my vulnerability. And often, someone reads it and recognizes themselves. We are all alone in our heads, but a well-chosen word can bridge that gap.

For me, writing is not about being perfect. It is about being true.
